items.title: CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager
items.description: Better Collective is looking for an experienced CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager to establish and lead a group-wide approach to customer relationship management across our portfolio of global sports media brands. This is a senior role combining CRM strategy, customer lifecycle management, technology, data, commercial thinking and operational leadership . The successful candidate will move CRM beyond campaign execution and develop it as a strategic capability that helps Better Collective build deeper, more valuable relationships with its audiences. Working across Product, Audience, Data, Commercial, Editorial, Technology and local brand teams, the CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager will create the frameworks, programmes and operating model required to turn first- and zero-party audience data into personalised customer experiences and measurable business value. The Opportunity Better Collective reaches millions of sports fans across a diverse portfolio of digital brands. The next stage of our audience strategy is to develop stronger direct relationships with those users — moving from anonymous audiences → known users → understood customers → engaged and valuable relationships . CRM will be central to that transformation. The CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager will establish the strategy, capabilities and standards that allow Better Collective brands to acquire, activate, engage, retain and monetise audiences across the customer lifecycle. Key Responsibilities CRM Strategy & Leadership Develop Better Collective's group-wide CRM and lifecycle strategy. Establish CRM principles, standards and best practices across brands. Create a scalable operating model balancing central CRM expertise with local brand execution. Identify where CRM can deliver the greatest audience and commercial impact. Build CRM roadmaps for priority Better Collective brands. Act as the senior CRM subject-matter expert across the organisation. Customer Lifecycle Management Design lifecycle strategies covering: Acquisition → Registration → Onboarding → Engagement → Conversion → Retention → Reactivation Develop automated programmes including: Welcome and onboarding journeys Profile completion Content discovery Personalised sports and player updates Newsletter engagement Subscription conversion Premium product promotion Renewal Retention Churn prevention Lapsed-user reactivation Win-back programmes The objective is to create relevant, personalised experiences rather than simply increase communication volume. First & Zero-Party Data Activation Work closely with Audience, Product and Data teams to translate Better Collective's growing first- and zero-party data capabilities into meaningful customer experiences. Use behavioural, declared and transactional data to improve: Audience segmentation Personalisation Content recommendations Lifecycle triggers Subscription propensity Retention Cross-sell opportunities Audience insight Help establish the connection between data capture, customer understanding and CRM activation . Multi-Channel CRM Develop a coordinated CRM approach across: Email Newsletters App push Web push In-app messaging On-site messaging Emerging direct audience channels Establish channel roles, contact strategies, frequency management and customer communication principles. Ensure customers receive coordinated experiences rather than disconnected messages from individual channels. CRM Technology & Automation Partner with Product and Technology teams to maximise Better Collective's CRM technology stack. Responsibilities include: Marketing automation Journey orchestration Audience segmentation Triggered communications Dynamic content Personalisation CRM/CDP integration Data flows Preference management Testing frameworks Reporting requirements Help translate business and customer requirements into practical technology capabilities. Measurement & Optimisation Create a consistent CRM measurement framework across Better Collective. Core metrics should include: Known-user growth Registration conversion Newsletter acquisition Email engagement Push engagement Active-user frequency Subscription conversion Renewal Retention Reactivation Revenue per known user Customer lifetime value Move CRM measurement beyond opens and clicks toward customer behaviour and commercial outcomes . Experimentation Establish a structured CRM experimentation programme covering: A/B testing Send frequency Timing Content Segmentation Personalisation Offers Lifecycle triggers Channel combinations Create mechanisms for successful experiments to be documented and scaled across Better Collective brands. Stakeholder Leadership CRM at Better Collective sits across multiple disciplines. The CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager will therefore work closely with: Audience — audience strategy, segmentation and zero/first-party data Product — registration, logged-in experiences and product journeys Data & BI — customer data, segmentation and measurement Technology — CRM platforms, integrations and automation Editorial — content propositions and newsletters Commercial — monetisation and customer value Subscription Teams — acquisition, renewal and retention Compliance — consent, GDPR, PECR and data governance Strong stakeholder leadership will be critical to the success of the role. We are looking for an experienced CRM leader who combines strategic thinking with the ability to turn strategy into operational programmes. The successful candidate will ideally have: Significant experience leading CRM, lifecycle or customer engagement programmes. Strong knowledge of email marketing and marketing automation. Experience developing sophisticated customer lifecycle strategies. Strong understanding of customer segmentation and personalisation. Experience working with large customer databases. Experience using behavioural and transactional data to improve communications. Strong understanding of CRM technology and platform capabilities. Experience working across Product, Data, Technology, Marketing and Commercial teams. Excellent stakeholder management skills. Experience managing CRM teams, agencies or specialist partners. Strong analytical and commercial mindset. Demonstrable experience connecting CRM activity to measurable business outcomes. Experience within digital media, subscriptions, publishing, sports, gaming or high-frequency digital consumer products would be particularly valuable. Leadership Profile The role requires someone who can operate at both strategic and practical levels. You should be comfortable moving between: Strategy ↔ Execution Customer ↔ Commercial Data ↔ Communications Technology ↔ Marketing Central Strategy ↔ Local Brand Requirements You will need to influence senior stakeholders while also being comfortable working directly with teams responsible for delivering CRM programmes. What Success Looks Like First 3 Months Audit CRM capabilities across priority Better Collective brands. Establish baseline CRM KPIs. Map existing lifecycle communications. Identify immediate optimisation opportunities. Define the group CRM strategy and operating principles. Prioritise brands and lifecycle use cases. 3–6 Months Launch priority automated lifecycle programmes. Establish group segmentation principles. Introduce a structured CRM experimentation framework. Establish CRM dashboards and commercial measurement. Develop CRM playbooks that can be reused across brands. 6–12 Months Better Collective has a scalable CRM capability connecting: Audience Data → Customer Insight → Segmentation → Personalisation → Activation → Measurement → Commercial Value CRM becomes a measurable growth engine supporting: Audience Engagement | Registration | Subscription | Retention | Revenue | Customer Lifetime Value Why This Role Matters Better Collective already has significant global audience scale. The opportunity is to build stronger direct relationships with those audiences. This role will help Better Collective transition from primarily understanding what audiences consume to understanding who our customers are, what they value and how we can build longer-lasting relationships with them . The CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager will be central to making that transition happen.

items.title: Research Engineer, Latency & Throughput
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a Research Engineer on the Latency & Throughput team, you will push the frontier of LLM inference by researching and prototyping techniques that reduce latency and increase throughput — from speculative decoding and quantization to KV compression and new attention variants. The team sits at the intersection of research and production: you will take ideas from recent literature, form hypotheses, run experiments, and ship the techniques that prove out into our serving stack. This role sits between our inference engineers, who own the production serving stack, and our research scientists, who focus on paper-level contributions. You will be more science-focused than a pure engineer: you are expected to generate new ideas, keep up with the state of the art, and implement proof-of-concepts that bridge the gap between academic results and production impact. Some techniques you explore will be lossy or require integration into training — retraining models, tuning architectures, or training auxiliary models to improve inference. You will work closely with the Inference Foundation and Kernels teams, who turn your validated techniques into production recipes, and with pretraining and RL teams when your work touches model training. Success is measured by demonstrated latency or throughput gains, first at small scale, then adopted in production. What You Will Do - Research and prototype inference techniques — speculative decoding, quantization, KV compression, watermarking, and new model architectures — by reading recent literature and forming testable hypotheses. - Design and run experiments to validate or refute ideas, iterating quickly on small-scale setups before proposing production integration. Demonstrate clear latency or throughput gains without unacceptable quality loss. - Collaborate with the Inference Foundation team to integrate validated techniques into the vLLM-based serving stack. - Partner with pretraining and RL teams when techniques require co-training, retraining, or training auxiliary models to improve inference. Build the right tooling and validation platforms to facilitate AI-driven inference research. What We're Looking For - A strong ML background with solid knowledge of LLM training techniques — architecture, tokenization, fine-tuning, and evaluation. - Hands-on experience with Python and PyTorch; you write clean, experimental code and iterate fast. JAX is acceptable with strong Python proficiency. C++ and Rust are not required, CUDA and GPU knowledge is expected but hands-on experience is not required. - Research experience of some form: a thesis, publications, a dedicated research project, or efficiency-oriented work in a lab or industry research setting. A PhD is not required, but we are looking for genuine research depth. - A track record of conducting experiments: forming hypotheses, designing controlled comparisons, and drawing clear conclusions from results. - Familiarity with the state of the art in LLM inference — you know what has been tried, what works, and where the open problems are. - Self-starter, low-ego, and collaborative. You are comfortable with ambiguity, negative results, and are eager to take matters into your own hands. - Inference or serving experience is a plus, not a requirement. Prior work with vLLM, production LLM deployments, or serving systems will help you ramp up faster. Location and Remote This role is based in our Paris or London offices (hybrid). We will prioritize candidates who reside in the Paris area or are open to relocating. We strongly believe in the value of in-person collaboration to foster strong relationships and seamless communication within our team. For senior profiles, we will also consider remote candidates based in France. In that case, we ask all new hires to visit our Paris office: - For the first week of their onboarding (accommodation and travel covered) - Then at least 3 days per month WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. items.title: Engineering Lead – AI Enablement (m/f/d)
items.description: Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market. Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns. Team AI Enablement builds Raisin's internal AI platform. We make it easy and safe for every team, from engineering and product to business operations, to use AI in their daily work and in the products they build. We provide the shared foundation for that: governed access to AI models and tools, the controls that keep data secure and usage auditable, and the visibility teams need to run AI reliably and cost-effectively. We also shape how Raisin builds software with AI, from AI-assisted coding to agentic workflows that support teams across the development lifecycle. Because Raisin operates in regulated financial services, security and compliance are core to how we design the platform. The team is growing, and you will shape both what it builds and how it works. Your Responsibilities As Engineering Lead, you lead the engineers who build Raisin's internal AI platform and drive the company's AI-assisted engineering practices. You are accountable for the team's delivery, growth, and maintaining the AI platform users' trust. You stay close to the technology, because in a field that changes this quickly, good leadership decisions depend on understanding the technical details. Lead and grow the team Hire, onboard, and develop engineers, and build a team that works autonomously across platform engineering, infrastructure, and AI. Hold regular 1:1s, set clear expectations, and agree individual development plans with each engineer. Give timely feedback, recognise strong performance, and address low performance early. Create an environment of trust, open communication, and continuous learning, so the team keeps up with a fast-moving field without burning out. Own delivery and operations Own end-to-end delivery, from planning and estimation through implementation and release, balancing new capabilities with reliability and maintenance. Make sure the platform runs well in production: on-call, incident handling, and service levels for the systems other teams rely on. Spot risks and blockers early and resolve them, or escalate in time with a clear proposal. Turn the AI strategy into quarterly goals and a roadmap the team commits to, together with your manager and stakeholders. Run the platform as a product Work with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to understand their needs and decide what the platform should offer next. Measure adoption, reliability, cost, and impact, and use that data in planning and when reporting to leadership. Manage the cost of AI usage and tooling, including budgets, licences, vendor relationships, and build-versus-buy decisions. Shape the technical direction Work with the team's tech leads on architecture and key technical decisions, and stay hands-on in design discussions, reviews, and selected implementation work. Work with security, legal, and compliance colleagues to keep the platform and the company's use of AI secure and compliant. Help engineering teams across Raisin adopt AI in their work through documentation, workshops, and direct support. Your Profile What you bring 3+ years leading engineers as an Engineering Manager, Engineering Lead, or Team Lead, including hiring and performance management. 7+ years in software engineering overall, with a background in backend, platform, infrastructure, or developer tooling. Experience leading a team that builds for internal customers, such as a platform, developer tooling, or shared services used by other engineers. A track record of delivering production systems that other teams depend on, including ownership of their reliability. A practical understanding of modern AI integration, such as LLM APIs, AI coding assistants, and agentic workflows, deep enough to evaluate technical decisions and challenge the team. You use AI tools in your own work. Clear communication with engineers, product, and business stakeholders, and fluency in English. Nice to have Experience with AI platform topics such as model access, governance, observability, rate limiting, or cost management. You have driven adoption of new tools or practices across an engineering organisation. Experience leading distributed or hybrid teams. Experience in a regulated industry such as banking or fintech. You don't need to tick every box. If you have led a platform or developer-tooling team and you are excited about what AI changes for engineering, we would like to hear from you. Join our mission, join our team – and grow with us! At Raisin, we care about each other and it is one of our top priorities to foster an open and caring environment in which everyone feels welcome and comfortable. Our culture is strongly driven by our ambitious team, which connects more than 75 different nationalities. As part of our team, you will benefit from: Employee Development Budget of €2,000 and four full training days per year. Flexible working hours, home office and 30 vacation days. A company pension scheme (Betriebliche Altersvorsorge), which we support with 20%. Enjoy more than 50+ different sports with Urban Sports Club: We subsidize your membership with more than €20 per month. Do you miss being in the office? The Deutschland Ticket gets you there, which we subsidize with €25 per month. Love cycling? With JobRad, lease the bike of your choice and enjoy tax savings, plus Raisin covers your monthly insurance costs. Hungry all the time? Snacks, daily fresh fruit as well as drinks provided at the office. You are moving from another country or city to join us? We may support your relocation. Raisin Applicant Privacy Policy We value diversity and the unique experiences each individual brings. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or gender identity.

items.location_text: New York, New York, United States
items.description: Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market. Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns. Team The Design team at Raisin brings together product designers and brand & marketing designers. We are united by a shared belief in respect, creativity, and our purpose to give people financial peace of mind. As our Digital Brand Designer, you'll join the Brand & Acquisition team. We shape how Raisin looks, moves, and feels across every market we operate in: paid and organic social, our websites, product launches, and campaigns. You'll report to the Head of Brand and Marketing Design and work integrated with the US Marketing team. Your main focus is conversion: designing and testing the landing pages, web journeys, and creative that turn interest into sign-ups. You'll also support broader marketing initiatives across paid social, web, and email, so Raisin feels consistent across the funnel. Your Responsibilities Conversion-Driven Web Design: Design, test, and optimize high-converting landing pages, reusable UI components, and end-to-end user journeys that elevate the brand and drive growth, while governing overall website design standards and brand alignment. Data-Informed Experimentation & Testing: Partner with Marketing to turn hypotheses into A/B and multivariate tests, from concept to shipped variant, and iterate based on the results, using funnel analytics, heatmaps, test results, and customer insights to find friction and decide what to test next. Creative Production: Produce static and animated creative, from hero assets to fast, iterative test variations within our brand design. Email & CRM: Design email templates and email campaigns with the CRM team, from lifecycle journeys to product launches. Templates & Systems: Build and maintain reusable templates, modules, and patterns for web, ads, and email, working with Product Design and the Raisin Design System so marketing and product feel like one brand. End-to-End Ownership: Act as a solution-oriented design partner, independently guiding cross-functional stakeholders from problem to execution, taking projects from brief to launch, including prototypes and leveraging AI for implementation-ready tests. Stakeholder Management: Present and explain design decisions with confidence, connecting them to the brand, the customer, and the business result. Workflow Innovation: Use AI tools across concepting, variant production, prototyping, test-implementation and analysis to work faster and test more, without compromising visual quality or compliance. Your Profile 4+ years in digital, marketing or web design, ideally in-house at a fintech, DTC or fast-growing tech company, or at an agency with performance clients. A portfolio that shows strong visual craft across brand, web, landing pages, paid social and email, and that tells the story behind the work: the problem, the hypothesis, what you tested and what changed. Proven experience designing for conversion. You have worked with growth or performance teams and know how to balance brand expression with commercial results. A data-informed mindset. You are comfortable reading test results and analytics, and you use them to make better design decisions. Excellent typography, layout and hierarchy skills, with attention to spacing, rhythm and detail. Expert in Figma, including components, auto layout and prototyping. Solid skills in Adobe Creative Suite. Practical use of AI in your design process today, for exploration, variant production or prototyping, not only for generating imagery. Hands-on ability to build implementation-ready components and code snippets (HTML/CSS) to deploy tests directly with marketing via Optimizely and Bloomreach. Speed without sloppiness. You can manage several projects at once in a fast-moving, feedback-rich environment. Clear communication in English, written and spoken. You can present and defend your work to stakeholders. Working knowledge of HTML/CSS, or experience with AI-assisted coding tools (for example Cursor, v0 or Claude Code). Experience with experimentation tools (for example Optimizely) and analytics tools such as Google Analytics, Hotjar or Looker. Nice to have Experience in financial services or another regulated industry, where trust and compliance shape the work. Basic motion design skills (After Effects, Jitter, Lottie, Figma Motion, or similar) for ads and web. Join our mission, join our team – and grow with us! At Raisin, we care about each other and it is one of our top priorities to foster an open and caring environment in which everyone feels welcome and comfortable. Our culture is strongly driven by our ambitious team, which connects more than 75 different nationalities. As part of our team, you will benefit from: Flexible working hours and up to 28 days PTO accrued from your first month, plus 13 public holidays. Employee Development Budget of $2,200 and 4 full training days per year. Company 401k contribution of 5%. Healthcare coverage contribution, including medical, dental and vision. Commuter benefits and flexible working from home policy. Regular team events and yearly Summer and Winter Party Salary Range $105,000 — $120,000 USD Raisin Applicant Privacy Policy We value diversity and the unique experiences each individual brings. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of race, colour, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, or gender identity.

items.title: Applied AI Engineer, Digital Natives
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineering teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Production-ready deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere. About the Role As an Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with leading organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work on consequential real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role is based in Paris. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees In this role, you will: - Partner directly with enterprise and digital native customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria. - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes. - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators. - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance. - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution. - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact. - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback. - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, product engineering or technical consulting. - Are fluent in both French and English - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or engineering of production systems—not only program or stakeholder management. - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable. - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment. - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost. - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes. - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives. - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments. - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://form.asana.com/?d=57018692298241&k=5MqR40fZd7jlxVUh5J-UeA. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link https://form.asana.com/?k=bQ7w9h3iexRlicUdWRiwvg&d=57018692298241. OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy https://cdn.openai.com/policies/global-employee-and-contractor-privacy-policy.pdf At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

items.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, VectorDB
items.location_text: New York City, NY | Seattle, WA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is looking for a Staff+ Software Engineer to work on the vector search infrastructure behind Claude. Retrieval is how Claude learns about the world. Web search across claude.ai, the API and agentic surfaces, memory across conversations, and the reinforcement learning workloads that train our next models all depend on fast, cheap, high-recall nearest-neighbor search over billions of vectors. You'll join a small team responsible for the vector database layer that serves Claude's retrieval workloads: its architecture, performance, scalability and cost. This is a foundational role. The team is small, core architectural decisions are still open, and the engineers who join now will shape how the system evolves. The role sits in our Databases organization and works day to day with the Search Platform team, which owns web search indexing, retrieval and serving, and the Memory & Search team, which owns search and memory inside claude.ai. We're looking for someone who has built vector or search systems that ran in production, at scale, with real users and a real on-call. You'll be hands-on in the code, and you'll also be the person deciding how the pieces fit together. Key responsibilities Own the core of Anthropic's vector database layer: index structures, storage layout, query execution and the serving layer Own production readiness - benchmarking against exact search, capacity planning, onboarding new workloads, and the operational tooling to run it at scale Drive the recall, latency and cost trade-offs - quantization, filtered search, index build and refresh strategy, and how compute and storage are separated and scaled Scale throughput by an order of magnitude as research and training demand grows, and work out whether the bottleneck is architecture, hardware or engineering bandwidth Extend the retrieval stack toward hybrid retrieval - lexical search and fused ranking alongside vector search Set the evaluation methodology for the system - recall targets, latency objectives, cost per query, and the regression detection that keeps them honest Set technical direction for a growing team - lead design reviews, make architectural decisions others build on, and mentor the engineers joining the effort Share the on-call for the systems you own Minimum qualifications Direct experience building a vector database or approximate nearest-neighbor search system that ran in production at scale Deep knowledge of ANN index structures (graph-based, clustering-based or disk-resident approaches), vector quantization and filtered search Experience with search relevance and ranking Strong systems programming skills in a language such as Rust, C++ or Go, including performance-critical and memory-intensive code Experience designing and operating large-scale distributed storage or serving systems with strict latency and reliability requirements A track record of independently scoping and delivering ambiguous, multi-quarter technical projects Strong written and verbal communication, with experience driving alignment across teams with different priorities Interest in AI safety and Anthropic's mission Preferred qualifications Experience with object-storage-backed or disaggregated compute and storage database designs Experience building or operating full-text search engines (inverted indexes, BM25) or hybrid retrieval systems Familiarity with embedding models and the retrieval demands of LLM training and inference Experience using GPUs or other accelerators for index build or search Prior experience as a technical lead on a database or search infrastructure team The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. items.title: Technical Program Manager, AI Delivery for Public Sector & Defense, Germany
items.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why This Role? We're seeking an experienced Program Manager to join Cohere's customer-facing Program Management team, with a focus on public sector and defence accounts in Europe, particularly in Germany. This is a highly specialised role requiring an individual who understands technical program delivery, the technical complexity of frontier AI models and the unique requirements of government and defence organisations. You will be the critical bridge between our cutting-edge AI capabilities and the specific needs of Ministries, Agencies, and defence organisations across Europe. You'll navigate complex procurement processes, stringent security requirements, data sovereignty concerns, and regulatory compliance while ensuring our customers successfully deploy and scale our AI solutions. In this role, you'll collaborate with our Strategic Customer team, Applied ML (AML) Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE), Platform, Product, and Go-to-Market teams, serving as the technical program lead and trusted advisor for our most sensitive and high-impact government and defence engagements. Location: Germany Eligibility: This individual must be a German citizen living in Germany and fluent in German, enabling immediate engagement with critical defense and national security customers. Security Clearance: German security clearance is not required, but is a strong nice-to-have. What You'll Do Customer Program Leadership: - Own end-to-end technical program delivery for Germany and broader European public sector and defence customers, from initial deployment through production scaling - Serve as the primary technical program point of contact for customers, building trusted relationships with departmental CIOs, IT directors, and technical teams - Translate complex public sector and defence requirements (security, compliance, accessibility, bilingualism, data sovereignty) into actionable engineering plans - Navigate complex procurement processes, RFP responses, and contractual technical obligations. Strategic Communication: - Provide clear, timely, and objective communication across Cohere's engineering organisation, customer stakeholders, pubic sector and defence leadership - Translate between AI/ML technical concepts and government-appropriate language for decision-makers who may not have deep technical backgrounds - Present technical roadmaps and status updates to senior stakeholders including departmental executives - Represent Cohere's technical capabilities in sensitive government and defence contexts. Complex Program Management: - Create and manage project schedules that account for public sector and defence timelines, security review processes, and approval cycles - Identify and manage dependencies across government departments, security authorities, cloud service providers, and internal Cohere teams - Navigate risks unique to government and defence deployments: privacy compliance, security, political and regulatory, technology and infrastructure. - Drive alignment between product development priorities and specific customer requirements. Technical Delivery & Execution: - Ensure on-time delivery of AI solutions that meet security, privacy, accessibility, and performance standards - Coordinate technical work across multiple teams: model customisation, security hardening, integration with government systems, bilingual support - Establish governance checkpoints appropriate for high-stakes government and defence deployments - Problem-solve complex technical challenges in air-gapped, on-premises, or highly regulated environments. You May Be a Good Fit If: Required Experience: - 6+ years of experience as a customer-facing Technical or Engineering Program Manager in AI/ML consulting, technology transformation, or enterprise software delivery. - Excellent executive communication and stakeholder management. - Experience working with government, defence, or heavily regulated customers. - Proven track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder technical programs with stringent compliance requirements. - Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; advanced degree or technical certs a plus. Technical Background: - Strong understanding of enterprise software deployment architectures (cloud, on-premises, hybrid, air-gapped) - Working knowledge of or experience with modern AI: LLMs, agentic systems, MCP, RAG, fine-tuning, evals, and responsible AI would be a strong differentiator - Comfortable discussing API integrations, model inference, data pipelines, and ML operations with technical stakeholders. Government & Defence Acumen: - Deep understanding of how government and defence organisations procure, evaluate, and deploy technology - Familiarity with European government requirements: data sovereignty, privacy laws (Privacy Act), accessibility standards, official languages obligations, security classifications - Understanding of defence and national security considerations in AI deployment - Experience with Algorithmic Impact Assessments or AI ethics frameworks is a strong asset - Eligible to obtain a German security clearance Nice to Have: - Active German security clearance - Bilingual (English/German) proficiency - Background in or strong familiarity with European defence, intelligence, or critical infrastructure sectors - Experience with GC Cloud services (Azure, AWS GovCloud) or Protected B/C environments - Project management certification (PMP, PgMP) or government-specific methodologies. Security Clearance Requirements This role strongly prefers eligibility for German government security clearance. We are looking for candidates eligible for German government clearance, meaning that they require German citizenship. In addition, this individual is required to be based in Germany and be fluent in German as this will enable immediate engagement with critical defence and national security customers. What Makes This Role Unique This isn't typical program management - it's a highly specialised role at the intersection of frontier AI, national security, and public sector digital transformation. You'll work on some of Canada's most sensitive and impactful AI deployments, helping government organisations harness cutting-edge technology while maintaining the highest standards of security, ethics, and accountability. If you're passionate about responsible AI adoption, understand the unique constraints and opportunities within government, and want to have an outsized impact on how Canada leverages AI to serve its citizens, this role is for you. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.description: ABOUT ELEVENLABS ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology. We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always. We have expanded from voice into three main platforms: - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale. - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages. - ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you. HOW WE WORK - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy. - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you. - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. items.title: Agent Post-Training, Computer Use Research
items.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Agent Post-Training team creates the frontier agents OpenAI ships to the world. We are training the models behind our agents in Codex, ChatGPT, the API, and other frontier products: persistent, proactive intelligence that can operate computers, collaborate with people and other agents, and expand what people and organizations can imagine, attempt, and achieve. We define what the next generation of agents should be able to do, build the training signal that teaches those abilities, and run the experiments that make them real. Our work spans coding, tool use, computer use, multi-agent coordination, long-horizon execution, factuality, instruction following, calibrated reasoning, and taste. Our team is where new model capabilities get made. We build the data, environments, graders, training methods, and feedback loops that shape what OpenAI's next agents can do, then carry those capabilities through major training runs and into the products people use. ABOUT THE ROLE As a member of Agent Post-Training, Computer Use, you will teach models to operate computers. You will help train models that can navigate browsers and desktops, use tools and applications, reason through complex workflows, collaborate with users and other agents, and complete long-horizon tasks with reliability and judgment. This work sits at the intersection of frontier model training, product behavior, evaluation, and systems engineering, and will directly shape the computer-use capabilities shipped in OpenAI’s next generation of agents. Currently, our models are the best in the world at this behavior! You will work with researchers, engineers, product teams, infrastructure teams, and safety/alignment partners to decide what should go into major model runs, measure whether it worked, and ship improvements into products used by real people. This is a high-agency role for people who want their work to land directly in frontier models. IN THIS ROLE, YOU MIGHT - Design and run experiments that improve agentic model behavior for complex computer use https://openai.com/index/codex-for-almost-everything/, including desktop and browser. - Own end-to-end improvements to the post-training stack, including RL, data pipelines, graders, reward signals, evals, diagnostics, and model-behavior analysis. - Build evals and environments that expose the next set of model failures, then turn those failures into training data, product fixes, or new research directions. - Partner with Codex and ChatGPT product teams to understand what users need and translate product signal into model improvements. - Work on early-training and alignment interventions, including data mixtures, objectives, synthetic data, and eval loops that shape downstream agent behavior. - Help decide which integrations, capabilities, and fixes are ready for inclusion in major model runs. - Improve the machinery for large-scale training and launch: experiment velocity, reliability, observability, reproducibility, cost, latency, and production readiness. - Take on cross-functional projects that touch model training, product infrastructure, and the production agent harness, such as multi-agent systems or training directly against production-like environments. - Debug hard failures in shipped or near-shipped models and turn messy qualitative behavior into concrete hypotheses, experiments, and fixes. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have strong technical fundamentals in machine learning, software engineering, systems, statistics, or a related field, and can learn quickly across the parts you have not worked in before. - Have hands-on experience with LLMs, RL, RLHF/RLAIF, post-training, evals, graders, synthetic data, model training, coding agents, tool-using agents, or production ML systems. - Are excited by open-ended problems where the path is unclear, the signal is noisy, and the right answer requires both research taste and engineering execution. - Care about product impact and model behavior, not just benchmark movement. You have opinions about what makes an agent useful, reliable, honest, tasteful, and easy to work with. - Can move from a vague behavioral problem to a concrete experiment: define the hypothesis, build the pipeline, run the model, analyze the result, and decide what to do next. - Are comfortable working across research, product, infrastructure, data, evals, and safety boundaries, and can communicate clearly with each group. - Like building load-bearing systems and processes when that is what the team needs, even if the work is not glamorous. - Want to train and ship the models that make agents genuinely useful for developers, enterprises, researchers, and everyday users. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's customer-facing teams are often the first place a customer sees what Claude can do. As a Demo Engineer, you'll build the demos, reference implementations, and reusable tooling that help those teams make new capabilities tangible, relevant, and trustworthy, ideally within days of a product launch rather than weeks after. This role sits between product engineering, technical storytelling, and GTM execution. You'll own ambiguous, high-leverage problems end to end: prototyping an agentic experience for a new capability, then hardening it into something reliable that other teams can run on their own. You'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and our sales and solutions teams, and you'll bring what you learn from customer-facing work back to the people building the products. Because a demo is frequently someone's first impression of what our models can and can't do, accuracy and honesty matter as much as polish. Success in this role looks like customer-facing teams demonstrating new capabilities sooner and with more confidence, recurring requests becoming reusable assets rather than one-off projects, and field insights shaping product and launch-readiness decisions. Responsibilities Own demo readiness for new and priority Claude capabilities, including environments, integrations, synthetic data, evaluations, reliability checks, and fallback paths Build prototypes, agents, and reference flows that make complex capabilities concrete and tie them to clear customer outcomes Turn recurring requests into reusable accelerators such as companion apps, templates, Skills, plugins, and self-service demo packages that scale across customer-facing teams Partner with GTM colleagues on high-impact customer moments, unblock critical technical gaps, and spot the patterns worth turning into shared assets Build internal agentic systems that automate demo preparation, validation, and asset maintenance, so demos stay current as products change Translate patterns from customer-facing work into product feedback, launch-readiness priorities, and systemic improvements with Product and Engineering Define and raise the bar for demo quality across accuracy, safety, reliability, usability, and adoption Decide when a customer need calls for a bespoke build and when it should become a shared capability You may be a good fit if you have Proficiency in Python or TypeScript, with experience shipping working software end to end Hands-on experience building applications or agents on top of LLM APIs, including prompting, tool use, and retrieval Experience designing integrations with third-party APIs, data sources, and services The ability to take an ambiguous capability or customer need to a working prototype quickly, and then make it reliable Clear communication of technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences, including sales and solutions teams Comfort collaborating across Product, Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and GTM teams Experience in a demo engineering, solutions engineering, sales engineering, forward deployed engineering, developer relations, or product engineering role A track record of building reusable internal tools, templates, or self-service assets that other teams adopted Hands-on experience with Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Skills, or plugins Experience building evaluation or validation harnesses for AI systems, including reliability checks and graceful fallbacks Experience building always-on or scheduled agentic systems that automate internal workflows Experience building synthetic or sanitized datasets that make demos realistic without exposing sensitive information Front-end or product design skills that help demos feel polished and intuitive Experience supporting product launches or running launch-readiness programs A history of turning field feedback into concrete product input that influenced a roadmap A passion for making powerful technology safe and beneficial, and a commitment to representing model capabilities accurately and honestly The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $240,000 — $315,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Audit, Security GRC
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY | Washington, DC
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the team Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments. We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them. We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits. Within Security GRC, Audit & Assurance runs the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework the program hangs off. This role sits in Audit & Assurance and helps run that integrated audit program, plan the audits we add next, and assess the frameworks and scope changes we are considering. About the role You'll help run Anthropic's unified audit program: quarterly audits across SOC 2, HIPAA and the ISO 27000 family including ISO 42001, plus the rest of our certifications, working with our audit firms, our GRC Partners, and control owners across the company. You'll plan new audits as we expand to new frameworks, platforms and regions, and run the gap assessments that tell us what each expansion takes before we commit to it. You'll help build the audit operating model and runbook, and drive automation in the program so evidence is collected once and reused across frameworks, requests reach control owners once, and each audit cycle takes less effort than the last. Building with Claude is a normal part of the job, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop. This is an individual contributor role for someone with program management experience who writes clearly, stays calm under deadlines, and likes making a busy program simpler. Key responsibilities Run the audit program as a program: one integrated plan and calendar across audits and expansions, with milestones, dependencies, risks and decisions tracked, and regular status to GRC leadership and stakeholders Plan and run the quarterly audits, from scoping through report and findings closeout Run audit readiness ahead of each fieldwork window: control owner prep, evidence pre-checks and walkthrough dry runs Scope each audit's boundary with Product and Engineering: which products and deployment paths are in scope, and flag when a launch or new platform changes it Help build the audit operating model and runbook for a unified audit program, and keep both current as the program grows Drive automation in the program: evidence collected from source systems, request tracking and audit reporting, with evidence and walkthroughs reused across frameworks Coordinate audits across frameworks and firms so audit windows line up and control owners are asked for the same evidence once, and drive new ways of automated evidence generation and collection with GRC Engineering Plan new audits and audit expansions as we commit to them Run framework and scope expansion evaluations and gap assessments, with a recommendation and an effort estimate leadership can act on Work closely with control owners and GRC Partners: prepare control owners for audits, get evidence delivered and findings closed, and hand findings that need extended remediation to GRC Partners Manage day-to-day auditor relationships, and report audit status, findings and program metrics to GRC leadership Minimum qualifications Several years of program management: running multi-workstream programs with a plan, milestones, dependencies, risk tracking and status reporting to leadership Several years running external security audits (SOC 2 and ISO 27001 at minimum), on the company side or at an audit firm, including seasons with several frameworks at once Working knowledge of SOC 2, the ISO 27000 family, ISO 42001 and HIPAA, and where their requirements overlap Experience leading a gap assessment for a new framework or scope change and presenting the result to leadership Experience building or improving an audit process: calendars, request tracking, runbooks, roles and responsibilities Enough technical fluency to understand how evidence is produced in cloud environments and to judge whether a system-generated report is complete and accurate, and to build simple automations with Claude Clear writing and calm coordination under deadline pressure Ability to get control owners to deliver on time without authority over them Preferred qualifications Audit firm experience (Big 4 or a SOC 2 or ISO certification body), especially as a senior or manager on technology clients Experience adding new frameworks such as PCI DSS, ISO 27701 or 27018, CSA STAR, or international schemes (for example IRAP, ISMAP or C5) Have automated evidence collection or audit reporting, or use Claude or other LLMs day to day to plan, track and report program work Experience with a GRC platform or building lightweight internal tooling You don't need to Have done everything on this list. The combination is running a global audit calendar well, plus the instinct to make it simpler each cycle Hold every certification. CISA, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor or similar are welcome but not required Have prior AI industry experience Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $255,000 — $270,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Director of Engineering, Clearing, Payments & Risk
items.description: ABOUT POLYMARKET Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market. In the US, Polymarket operates a CFTC-regulated exchange (DCM) and clearinghouse (DCO), and we're building the infrastructure to bring event contracts to a much wider set of customers and partners. Engineering here is small, senior, and close to the business: the systems you build move real money under real regulatory obligations. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring a Director of Engineering to lead the teams that move, clear, and protect customer funds on Polymarket US. You'll own our clearing, payments, and risk systems, and you'll lead engineering for our Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) build, one of the most important initiatives in the company. This role needs a manager who has built these systems before and understands the regulatory model behind them, not one who will learn it on the job. WHAT YOU'LL DO • Lead engineering for the FCM program end to end: customer onboarding and account structure, customer fund segregation, margin and collateral, and the integration between the FCM and our clearinghouse. • Own the clearing engine and the post-trade path: settlement, position and balance management, reconciliation, and the ledger that sits underneath all of it. • Own payments: deposits and withdrawals across bank, card, and wallet rails, fraud and risk checks at authorization, and the processor and banking partners behind them. • Build risk controls that run in real time: pre-trade and pre-funding checks, exposure limits, and the monitoring that tells us when something is wrong before a customer or regulator does. • Work daily with Clearing Operations, Treasury, Compliance, Legal, and the DCO/FCM business leads to turn regulatory and operational requirements into systems that hold up under audit. • Hire, grow, and manage a team of senior engineers. Set the technical bar, run on-call, and stay close enough to the code to make good design calls. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR • 8+ years in software engineering and 2+ years managing engineers, with a track record of shipping financial systems in production. • Direct subject-matter experience with at least two of: FCM operations, clearing and settlement, payments infrastructure. Ideally you've built these at an FCM, futures or crypto derivatives exchange, broker-dealer, or payments company. • Working knowledge of the CFTC framework for customer funds: segregation, margining, daily reconciliation and reporting, and what regulators expect from the systems that produce them. • Strong instincts for money-movement correctness: double-entry ledgers, idempotency, reconciliation, and failure handling across external partners. • Comfort leading a 0-to-1 build at startup speed while keeping the controls a regulated business needs. • Clear written communication with both engineers and non-technical partners in operations, finance, and compliance. •(Plus) Experience standing up a new FCM, DCO, or derivatives clearing member, or taking one through a regulatory review. •(Plus) Background with margin methodologies (for example SPAN-style models) or collateral management. •(Plus) Experience with stablecoin or on-chain settlement rails alongside traditional banking rails. •(Plus) Hands-on experience in Go or another systems language used for high-throughput services. BENEFITS - Competitive salary and equity - Unlimited PTO - Health, vision, and dental coverage - 401(k) match - Full hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, large display, and accessories PAY TRANSPARENCY Base salary range: $350,000 to $500,000 annually, plus equity and benefits. This range reflects a good-faith estimate for this position. Experience levels vary widely within a title here, so please reach out even if your expectations fall outside it. We're always happy to chat.
